A new court filing details the condition of the Tennessee woman who officials attempted to execute earlier this week.
Attorneys for Christa Pike say she was placed on a ventilator and remained unconscious as hospital staff worked to save her life and clear the drug the state had administered from her body.
Tony Gonzalez of member station WPLN reports.
Christa Pike's legal team wants the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence and is asking a judge for help.
They're also citing several months of warnings they had provided about a blood disorder that would make it difficult to insert an IV line.
They were also concerned because prison staff had failed to insert a line during another lethal injection attempt in May.
Now they say that the drug pentobarbital could have been sent into Pike's arm instead of her vein.
Tennessee has struggled with lethal injections.
Four years ago, officials were found to have ignored protocols and mishandled drugs.
The state made changes, but concerns remained and the governor has now ordered another review.
For NPR News, I'm Tony Gonzalez in Nashville.
On Wednesday, the Trump administration began mailing out $500 checks to almost one million Americans enrolled in certain private health insurance plans.
As NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports, the money comes from fees collected from health insurance companies.
The group of people receiving the checks live in one of the 30 states that use HealthCare.gov as their Obamacare website and make too much money to receive premium subsidies.
Cynthia Cox directs the program on the Affordable Care Act at the health research organization KFF.
Essentially what the Trump administration is doing is taking some user fee dollars that insurance companies have paid to the federal government to operate HealthCare.gov.
Usually that money is used for community groups who help people understand their options and enroll.
But the Trump administration has slashed funding for those groups and is now sending out checks instead.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
Democrats are expanding the map of congressional races they say could be winnable next month.
As NPR's Tamara Keith reports, the new list includes 66 districts.
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is pushing into traditionally Republican territory, adding districts in Kansas, North Carolina, Texas and Oklahoma among others to its districts in playlist.
That is a list of congressional districts where the party committee thinks it can be competitive.
It doesn't mean the Democratic candidates in these races have an easy path to victory, but it does mean Democrats are bullish about their chances overall.
Republicans are projecting confidence as well, with speaker Mike Johnson traveling around the country saying he thinks his party will expand its House majority.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
It was a good day on Wall Street Friday with stocks finishing up across the board.
The NASDAQ was up 1.2 percent. And you're listening to NPR News.
Stocks did rise following the latest job market update that cooled concerns that a potentially hot economy could make inflation worse.
The S&P 500 finished up seven-tenths of a percent and pulled within one percent of its record set in August.
The NASDAQ finished up 1.2 percent and the Dow Jones Industrials added half a percent.
The deal to merge Paramount's Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is expected to become final next week.
NPR's Mandalit Del Barco reports.
With help from his billionaire father Larry Ellison and investors from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and others,
David Ellison will soon have control over his mega company, which he named Skydance.
Ellison is spending more than $111 billion to combine two legacy film studios, streaming companies and news outlets CNN and CBS News.
What once was the peak is now just the beginning.
Ellison posted this video on X and wrote that Skydance will allow Paramount and Warner Bros. to continue their individual identities.
Despite protests from actors, writers and others, and after passing legal and regulatory challenges, the deal is expected to close on Tuesday.
Mandalit Del Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
Former Miami Congressman David Rivera has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for a secret $50 million lobbying campaign for Venezuela.
The Republican was found guilty in May of failing to register as a foreign agent and conspires a conspiracy to commit money laundering.
The lobbying campaign came during President Trump's first term in office.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
